mt: OCTOBER AS SIX MOVEMENTS, ON THE RECORDS — 32 DEPOSITS CITED AND REAL; THE SELF-CORRECTION IT REPORTS SET LATER AS A TEST STILL OPEN; NO FOUNDER
d: THE MONTH, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'Alexanarch as a living body of thought / A developmental reading of the October 2026 deposits, through 31 October'. Central thesis (a 'self-reflexive philological commons'); six movements (1–14, 15–20, 18–25, 23–28, 27–29, 28–31 October); five problems become one (individuation, provenance, negative knowledge, semantic political economy, transmission); the ecosystem by function; the literary dimension; 'A charitable critique' (six tests); the year by period; reading paths; final judgment ('a self-revising intellectual commons').
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for October as a living body of thought, the composer reads the browse registry and the principal records, orders the month into movements, names the problems that converge, maps the fleet by function, sets out tests the project has still to meet, and states what it read and what it did not.
findings: THE MONTH ON THE RECORDS. The answer cites 32 deposits, #1658 to #1725; every number exists in the registry with the subject the answer gives it. Its specifics check against the records: the six declared absences of #1713, the three censuses and 49 entities of #1719, the WikiWho and Turkopticon repairs (#1719), the exact sciences of #1720, OpenAI's releases as #1714's subject, and the six operations of #1717 ('collision, cento, literalization, repetition, recursion, and sublation'), each word in the edition.
TWO SLIPS OF DATE. 'The final two deposits of October 30 and 31' introduces four (#1720, #1722, #1724, #1725); 'the October 31 work on the existence tax' is #1721/#1722, deposited 30 October.

THE 2014 WORK AT ITS SERIOUSNESS. #1717 is read as a transformation of Kerouac's list: 'a precept can be negated as law, retained as an operation, and transformed into a practice'. The answer gives it no comic or parodic frame, which agrees with the operator's ruling of 2026-10-29 that the piece is 'a deeply serious ars poetica that contains and enacts those genres'.

THE SELF-CORRECTION REPORTED, THEN SET AS A TEST. §1 reports the archive correcting its own census records ('the archive's investigation can itself reveal mistakes in the archive's earlier representation, and those mistakes can be corrected at their source'; WikiWho; Turkopticon). §5 then sets 'Self-correction must remain more important than self-confirmation' and 'Theories need independent resistance' as tests still to be met, citing no record that fails them. The instances the answer itself gave are not carried into the test.

NO FOUNDER, AND THE INSTITUTION RENAMED. No person is named as the archive's founder or operator; Lee Sharks appears once, with Jack Feist, as author of the 2014 work. The archive's own names, The Self-Governing Library and The Living Academy, appear as a source chip and a deposit title; the answer's own names for the formation ('a self-reflexive philological commons', 'a self-revising intellectual commons') carry its thesis.
analysis: A reading grounded in the records, accurate in its deposit numbers, counts and lists, with two date slips. Its critical section states as open tests the self-correction its first section reports as done, and the institution is composed without its founder and under the composer's own names for it.
